title: Nanodisc-Tm: Rapid functional assessment of nanodisc reconstituted membrane proteins by CPM assay
author: Ashok, Jaakola
materials: 1-Palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphocholine (POPC) and 1-palmitoyl-2-oleoyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-l-serine (POPS) were purchased from Avanti Polar Lipids. We have used Bio-beads, Biorad and Amberlite XAD-2, Sigma–Aldrich with equal success.1.Solubilize lipids using sodium cholate detergent. Cholate concentration must be twice as lipid concentration. For example, solubilize 100 mM lipids in 200 mM cholate.2.Using PD-10 column buffer exchange the receptor to 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 800 mM NaCl and 0.01% DDM-CHS.3.Mix A2AR: Membrane Scaffold Protein 1D1 (MSP1D1): lipid in a ratio of 1:10:700. POPC:POPS (7:3) was used in reconstitution. POPS is a negatively charged lipid. This is added to mimic the negative charge of the inner leaflet of the plasma membrane. The above mentioned ratio has been optimized to yield monomeric adenosine A2A receptor in nanodiscs. Use His tag cleaved MSP1D1 protein.4.Incubate the mixture with wet bio beads (170 mg of beads for 250 μl reaction) overnight at 4 °C to capture detergents and to aid in nanodiscs formation. Next day puncture a hole in the bottom of the tube and place it in a 15 ml falcon tube. Centrifuge the falcon tube to collect the mixture.5.Pre-equilibrate IMAC resin with 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl and 25 mM imidazole. Use 200 μl Ni-NTA (nickel-nitrilotriacetatic acid) agarose column volume. His tag is present only in receptors and MSP1D1 does not have any His tag. Thus empty nanodiscs are removed in this step. Wash with 10 column volumes of 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl and 50 mM imidazole. Elute the bound proteins with 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl and 500 mM imidazole. This IMAC procedure effectively removes empty nanodiscs and purifies only nanodisc reconstituted receptors.6.Concentrate the eluted A2A receptor-nanodisc with a 30 kDa cut-off concentrator while simultaneously exchanging the buffer to 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl.7.As the above mentioned ratio is optimized for GPCR (G protein-coupled receptors) incorporation into nanodiscs, we rarely find any aggregation. Thus, we only run an analytical scale size exclusion chromatography for verification.8.Check reconstitution by SDS-PAGE and radioligand binding (if applicable).

steps.title: Prepare CHS/DDM solubilization mix
steps.instruction: Make a 2 % (w/v) cholesteryl hemi‑succinate (CHS) solution in 10 % (w/v) n‑dodecyl‑β‑d‑maltoside (DDM).

steps.title: Thaw membranes and add iodoacetamide
steps.instruction: Thaw the harvested Sf9 membranes on ice, add 4 mM theophylline, then add iodoacetamide to a final concentration of 2 mg ml⁻¹ and incubate at 4 °C for 30 min.

steps.title: Solubilize membranes and clarify
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume (2×) of solubilization buffer (50 mM Hepes pH 7.5, 1600 mM NaCl, 20 % glycerol, 2 % DDM‑CHS mixture, 4 mM theophylline) to the membranes, incubate at 4 °C for 2.5 h, then centrifuge at 150 000 g for 45 min to remove unsolubilized material.

steps.title: Bind receptor to TALON resin
steps.instruction: For each litre of biomass, add 1 ml of TALON (Clontech) IMAC resin pre‑equilibrated with the solubilization buffer; mix the clarified supernatant with the resin and incubate overnight at 4 °C in the presence of 20 mM imidazole.

steps.title: Wash and elute receptor from IMAC
steps.instruction: Wash the resin sequentially with 10 column volumes (CV) of wash buffer I (250 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 800 mM NaCl, 10 mM MgCl₂, 0.1 % DDM‑CHS, 10 % glycerol, 25 mM imidazole, 8 mM ATP, 100 µM ZM341285) and then 10 CV of wash buffer II (50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 800 mM NaCl, 0.05 % DDM‑CHS, 10 % glycerol, 50 mM imidazole, 100 µM ZM341285). Elute the bound receptor with elution buffer (25 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 800 mM NaCl, 0.01 % DDM‑CHS, 10 % glycerol, 220 mM imidazole, 100 µM ZM341285).

steps.title: Concentrate and assess purified receptor
steps.instruction: Concentrate the eluted receptor using a 100 kDa centrifugal concentrator and evaluate purity and monodispersity by SDS‑PAGE and analytical size‑exclusion chromatography (aSEC).

steps.title: Solubilize lipids with sodium cholate
steps.instruction: Dissolve POPC and POPS (Avanti) in sodium cholate at twice the lipid molarity (e.g., 100 mM total lipids in 200 mM cholate).

steps.title: Buffer exchange receptor to low detergent
steps.instruction: Exchange the purified receptor into 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 800 mM NaCl, 0.01 % DDM‑CHS using a PD‑10 desalting column.

steps.title: Mix receptor, MSP1D1, and lipids
steps.instruction: Combine receptor, MSP1D1 (His‑tag cleaved) and the cholate‑solubilized lipid mixture at a molar ratio of 1 : 10 : 700 (receptor : MSP1D1 : lipid) using a POPC:POPS composition of 7 : 3.

steps.title: Detergent removal with bio‑beads
steps.instruction: Add wet Bio‑Beads (170 mg per 250 µl reaction) to the mixture and incubate overnight at 4 °C to adsorb detergent and promote nanodisc formation.

substeps.instruction: Add wet Bio‑Beads (170 mg per 250 µl)

steps.title: Collect nanodisc mixture
steps.instruction: The next day, puncture the bottom of the reaction tube, place it into a 15 ml Falcon tube and centrifuge to collect the nanodisc suspension.

steps.title: Remove empty nanodiscs by IMAC
steps.instruction: Pre‑equilibrate a 200 µl Ni‑NTA agarose column with 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 25 mM imidazole; load the nanodisc mixture, wash with 10 CV of 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM imidazole, and elute bound receptor‑nanodiscs with 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 500 mM imidazole.

substeps.instruction: Wash (10 CV) with 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 50 mM imidazole

steps.title: Concentrate nanodisc‑reconstituted receptor
steps.instruction: Concentrate the eluted nanodisc‑reconstituted A2A receptor using a 30 kDa cutoff concentrator while simultaneously exchanging the buffer to 50 mM Hepes pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl.

steps.title: Verify reconstitution by SEC and SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Run an analytical size‑exclusion chromatography run and SDS‑PAGE (or radioligand binding if desired) to confirm monodispersity and successful reconstitution.
